boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-purchase campus and nearby activities with direct access evidence for Lake Forest College students.

cards.title: Settle into the Skybox Lounge
cards.subtitle: Mohr Student Center
cards.notes: Bring a friend, use the seating, tables, or TV, and check whether an organization has reserved the lounge after 4 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge for an easy daytime or evening pause.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College says students are welcome to use the Skybox Lounge and that during the day they are free to use it.
cards.access_notes: For Lake Forest College students; organizations may reserve the space after 4 p.m.

cards.title: Take a break in the CCP Lobby
cards.subtitle: Mohr Student Center
cards.notes: Use the lobby to rest, relax, or do homework; keep in mind that the office is working there during the day.
cards.short_summary: A relaxed Mohr Student Center stop that remains open into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College says students may freely use the Center for Chicago Programs lobby to rest, relax, and do homework.
cards.access_notes: For Lake Forest College students; the lobby is open through the evening after the offices close.

cards.title: Meet up in Calvin Durand Hall
cards.subtitle: Mohr Student Center
cards.notes: Choose this public campus space for a low-key conversation or homework session, then leave it ready for the next group.
cards.short_summary: A publicly usable space inside the Mohr Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College identifies Calvin Durand Hall in Mohr Student Center as one of the public campus spaces students are welcome to use.

cards.title: Choose a library study spot
cards.subtitle: 555 North Sheridan Road, Lake Forest
cards.notes: Pick an individual, collaborative, or group-study space and use the library as a quiet anchor for a planned meet-up.
cards.short_summary: Study and collaboration spaces at the center of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College lists the Donnelley and Lee Library among public campus spaces students are welcome to use and describes individual, collaborative, and group study spaces.
cards.source_title: Donnelley and Lee Library | Lake Forest College
cards.access_notes: For Lake Forest College students; building hours are listed separately by the College.

cards.entity_name: Brown Hall Collaboration and Quiet Spaces
cards.title: Work together in Brown Hall
cards.subtitle: Brown Hall, Middle Campus
cards.notes: Find an available collaboration or quiet space for a group task, and check first if a room needs a reservation.
cards.short_summary: Flexible Brown Hall spaces for quiet work or collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College states that Brown has collaboration and quiet spaces for student use and that most are available without a reservation.
cards.access_notes: For Lake Forest College students; most spaces are available without reservation.

cards.title: Use the Art Institute student admission
cards.subtitle: 111 S. Michigan Ave, Chicago
cards.notes: Bring your Lake Forest College ID and confirm current entry details with the College before traveling to the museum.
cards.short_summary: A College partnership provides student museum access without an admission purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College states that its students enjoy free admission to the Art Institute of Chicago 365 days a year through the University Partner relationship.
cards.source_title: College and Art Institute unite for cultural exploration | Lake Forest College
cards.access_notes: Lake Forest College student ID is required; verify museum entry procedures before the visit.

cards.title: Join First Connection before orientation
cards.subtitle: Lake Forest College campus
cards.notes: Eligible new students can use this pre-orientation program to meet peers and mentors while getting acquainted with campus.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost pre-orientation program for newly admitted students.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College says First Connection is free for participants and provides all activities and meals free of charge.
cards.access_notes: For newly admitted students participating in the pre-orientation program; the College lists August 19, 2026 move-in.

cards.title: Reserve a student theater ticket
cards.subtitle: Hixon Theater, South Campus
cards.notes: Check the theater page for the next production, reserve early when required, and bring College affiliation for the $0 ticket.
cards.short_summary: Campus theater performances with $0 tickets for College students.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Forest College lists tickets for its theater production as $0 for Lake Forest College students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: For Lake Forest College students, faculty, and staff; confirm the current production and reservation availability.

cards.title: Walk to Fort Sheridan’s lake overlook
cards.subtitle: Fort Sheridan Forest Preserve, Lake Forest
cards.notes: Follow the short paved Lake Overlook Trail from the Gilgare Lane lot and use the viewing area for a shoreline reset.
cards.short_summary: A paved walk to Lake Michigan views from a 70-foot bluff.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake County Forest Preserves describes Fort Sheridan as offering free public access to Lake Michigan and identifies the paved Lake Overlook Trail.
cards.source_title: Fort Sheridan Forest Preserve | Lake County Forest Preserves
cards.access_notes: Open daily 6:30 a.m. to sunset; use the Gilgare Lane parking lot for the Lake Overlook Trail.

cards.title: Walk Fort Sheridan’s Lake Michigan shoreline
cards.subtitle: Fort Sheridan Forest Preserve, Lake Forest
cards.notes: Stay on the permitted shoreline stretch, bring only what you carry out, and skip swimming, wading, and boating at this preserve.
cards.short_summary: A lakefront walk with free public access and a designated sandy shore.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake County Forest Preserves says Fort Sheridan offers free public access to Lake Michigan and permits walking along a 0.75-mile sandy shoreline stretch.
cards.source_title: Fort Sheridan Forest Preserve | Lake County Forest Preserves
cards.access_notes: Open daily 6:30 a.m. to sunset; swimming, wading, and boating are not allowed.
